metadata.title: ढुकू प्रथा कैसे अभिशाप बन गई | Changing Perception of Live-in Relationships in Tribal Society
metadata.description:
In many tribal communities across India, live-in relationships have been an accepted and traditional way of forming families. In Jharkhand, this practice is known as Dhuku Pratha, where a couple lives together before marriage, often gaining societal acceptance over time. However, with modernization, religious influences, and shifting social norms, this age-old tradition has increasingly been viewed with skepticism.

Our ground report delves into how Dhuku Pratha is gradually losing acceptance, particularly in urban and semi-urban tribal populations. We explore the role of external cultural influences, legal and religious interventions, and economic changes in reshaping societal attitudes. Through firsthand accounts and expert insights, we uncover why this once-respected tradition is now seen as a challenge to conventional morality. As tribal communities navigate between tradition and modernity, we ask: Is the decline of Dhuku Pratha a sign of progress, or the loss of cultural identity?
